title: Recurrent networks and sequence learning
blurb: Nando de Freitas explains recurrent networks, LSTMs, sequence-to-sequence learning, and attention in Oxford’s machine-learning course. The lecture captures the neural-language approaches researchers were developing before transformers, including translation and generating sequences one step at a time.
publisher: Nando de Freitas / University of Oxford

media.alt: Oxford lecture on recurrent neural networks and sequence learning

title: Making neural translation practical
blurb: Jacob Devlin explains the engineering of attention-based neural translation, from training large models to decoding their outputs efficiently. His research talk connects sequence-learning methods with the practical decisions needed to make translation systems useful.

media.alt: Jacob Devlin presents A Practical Guide to Neural Machine Translation at Microsoft Research

title: The transformer enters the conversation
blurb: Transformer coauthor Łukasz Kaiser presents attention-based neural networks at Pi School during the year of Attention Is All You Need. The talk captures the architecture’s early research context and its approach to processing sequences.

media.alt: Łukasz Kaiser presents deep-learning research at the Pi School launch

title: ULMFiT brings transfer learning to language
blurb: Jeremy Howard teaches language-model pretraining and transfer learning for text classification in the original fast.ai course. The lesson makes ULMFiT’s approach practical: adapt a pretrained language model to a particular collection of text and its labels.

media.alt: Jeremy Howard teaches NLP classification and language-model transfer learning

title: GPT-2 and open-ended text generation
blurb: Alec Radford discusses GPT-2 in his NeurIPS workshop presentation on transfer learning for text generation. The excerpt begins with GPT-2, showing how broad language-model training was changing the range of tasks researchers could attempt.

media.alt: Alec Radford discusses GPT-2 at the NeurIPS creativity workshop

title: GPT-3 learns from examples in the prompt
blurb: The original NeurIPS presentation of GPT-3 explains few-shot learning through examples supplied in a prompt. It describes a shared language-model interface for varied tasks, with evaluations covering translation, question answering, and other forms of text completion.

media.alt: Original NeurIPS presentation of Language Models Are Few-Shot Learners

title: Codex turns instructions into code
blurb: OpenAI demonstrates Codex translating natural-language instructions into working code during its live launch. The examples show a language model acting as an interface for software creation, with users describing changes and inspecting the generated program.

media.alt: OpenAI's live demonstration of Codex generating code from instructions

title: InstructGPT learns from human feedback
blurb: Lead author Long Ouyang presents InstructGPT and its use of human feedback to improve instruction following. The technical discussion explains how training can shape a language model’s responses toward the intent expressed by its user.

media.alt: Long Ouyang presents OpenAI's InstructGPT research and human-feedback training

title: GPT-4's developer demonstration
blurb: OpenAI’s GPT-4 developer livestream demonstrates the new model through coding and other tasks. The presentation shows developers testing its responses in concrete workflows and introduces the model’s ability to work with both language and visual input.

media.alt: OpenAI's GPT-4 developer livestream

title: GPT-4o brings voice and vision together
blurb: OpenAI introduces GPT-4o through demonstrations combining spoken interaction and visual input. The launch brings language models closer to a conversational interface that can respond to what a person says and shows during an exchange.

media.alt: OpenAI introduces GPT-4o with voice and vision demonstrations

title: GPT-5's reasoning and coding launch
blurb: OpenAI introduces GPT-5 through its original launch presentation and demonstrations. The event brings reasoning, coding, and broader assistance into a common product story, showing how the company expects people to use the model for increasingly involved tasks.

media.alt: OpenAI's original GPT-5 launch and demonstrations

title: GPT-6 Astra tackles longer computer tasks
blurb: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Astra with an emphasis on complex work, software engineering, and computer use across longer tasks. The launch shows the company’s approach to systems that carry instructions through extended workflows and multiple intermediate steps.

media.alt: OpenAI's official introduction of GPT-6 Astra

title: Atlas gets an untethered upgrade
blurb: DARPA introduces an upgraded Atlas ahead of the Robotics Challenge Finals. An onboard battery and revised hydraulic system prepare the platform for untethered operation, while changes to its arms, wrists, and sensing support more demanding disaster-response tasks.

media.alt: DARPA introduces the upgraded untethered Atlas robot

title: Atlas, the next generation
blurb: Boston Dynamics demonstrates a new Atlas walking outdoors, handling boxes, and recovering after disturbances. The selected research footage brings balance and manipulation into the same sequence, showing the robot adapting its movement as its surroundings change.

media.alt: Atlas walks, handles boxes, and recovers from disturbances

title: Atlas lands a backflip
blurb: Atlas jumps between platforms and completes a backflip in Boston Dynamics’ demonstration. The sequence brings takeoff, aerial motion, and landing into one coordinated maneuver, making the demands of dynamic whole-body control unusually visible.

media.alt: Atlas jumps between platforms and performs a backflip

title: Atlas takes on parkour
blurb: Atlas runs through a prepared obstacle course and climbs a sequence of elevated platforms. The demonstration connects perception with foot placement and balance, showing the robot carrying momentum through successive changes in height.

media.alt: Atlas runs and climbs through a parkour obstacle course

title: More parkour, longer movement sequences
blurb: Boston Dynamics presents Atlas combining jumps, turns, and gymnastic movements into a coordinated routine. Linking these motions extends the control problem beyond a single maneuver, requiring the robot to arrive in position for its next movement.

media.alt: Atlas combines dynamic movements in Boston Dynamics' More Parkour Atlas film

title: Whole-body control, choreographed
blurb: Atlas joins other Boston Dynamics robots in a choreographed dance. The prepared routine demonstrates coordinated motion and balance through an expressive sequence, making physical control legible through familiar movements and changes of rhythm.

media.alt: Atlas and other Boston Dynamics robots perform a choreographed dance

title: Atlas: partners in parkour
blurb: Two Atlas robots traverse a prepared parkour course in Boston Dynamics’ original demonstration. Linked movements bring perception, timing, and balance together, with each landing and transition setting up the next part of the routine.

media.alt: Two Atlas robots complete a linked parkour demonstration

title: Tesla presents its Optimus prototype
blurb: Tesla presents its Optimus prototype during AI Day 2022 and discusses the hardware and software behind the project. Playback begins at the Tesla Bot Demo chapter, capturing the public prototype milestone and the team’s engineering direction.

media.alt: Tesla demonstrates its Optimus humanoid prototype at AI Day 2022

title: Atlas gets a grip
blurb: Atlas carries and places objects while moving through a staged construction scenario. The demonstration combines locomotion with manipulation, requiring the robot to account for carried objects as it changes position and interacts with the prepared environment.

media.alt: Atlas combines object handling and movement in a staged construction demonstration

title: An all-electric Atlas
blurb: Boston Dynamics reveals an all-electric Atlas with a new mechanical design following its hydraulic research platform. The short film emphasizes joint motion and body configuration, introducing a different hardware foundation for the company’s humanoid work.

media.alt: Boston Dynamics reveals its electric Atlas humanoid

title: Learning Atlas locomotion with neural networks
blurb: Boston Dynamics demonstrates Atlas locomotion under end-to-end neural-network control. The footage connects learning-based methods with movement on a physical humanoid, showing how trained control policies can express coordinated behavior through the robot’s body.

media.alt: Boston Dynamics demonstrates Atlas locomotion with end-to-end neural networks

title: How Atlas learns
blurb: Boston Dynamics explains how Atlas learns in an original technical film. The presentation connects the training process with behavior on the physical robot, giving a view of the work behind demonstrations of useful skills.

media.alt: Boston Dynamics explains how Atlas learns robot skills

title: MIT Cheetah lands the running jump
blurb: MIT’s Cheetah detects and clears hurdles while running. The demonstration brings electric actuation, sensing, and dynamic control together, showing how the robot prepares a jump and returns to a running gait after landing.

media.alt: MIT Cheetah jumps over hurdles while running

title: Minitaur explores direct-drive legs
blurb: Ghost Robotics demonstrates early direct-drive Minitaur prototypes moving outdoors. The footage introduces a leg architecture built around direct motor actuation, showing its behavior through physical contact with terrain and changes in movement.

media.alt: Ghost Robotics' early direct-drive Minitaur prototypes move outdoors

title: Cassie's purpose-built bipedal legs
blurb: Oregon State introduces Cassie, a bipedal research platform with a distinctive leg architecture. The reveal shows the mechanical platform in motion, making leg geometry and balance central to the story of a robot built for walking research.

media.alt: Oregon State University introduces the Cassie bipedal robot

title: Cheetah moves without relying on vision
blurb: MIT demonstrates Cheetah traversing obstacles with control that operates through physical contact and internal sensing. The vision-free experiments highlight how actuation and feedback can support movement when a detailed visual model of the terrain is unavailable.

media.alt: MIT Cheetah negotiates obstacles without relying on vision

title: Mini Cheetah makes dynamic hardware modular
blurb: MIT’s Mini Cheetah performs agile movements and backflips using a small, modular research platform. Reusable actuator modules and replaceable components make the robot an example of hardware designed to support repeated experimentation with dynamic control.

media.alt: MIT Mini Cheetah demonstrates agile movement and a backflip

title: Open hardware for dynamic robots
blurb: The Open Dynamic Robot Initiative introduces shared robot designs and modular hardware for research. Its presentation shows the physical platforms and the approach to making their components reproducible, giving other teams a starting point for experimentation.

media.alt: Introduction to the Open Dynamic Robot Initiative and its robot hardware

title: Go1 packages quadruped hardware as a product
blurb: Unitree introduces Go1 in a product film showing a compact quadruped moving alongside people. The launch packages legged locomotion as a complete commercial platform, bringing sensing, actuation, control, and the robot body into one offering.

media.alt: Unitree's original Go1 quadruped launch film

title: B1 targets tougher operating conditions
blurb: Unitree presents B1 through demonstrations focused on load carrying and demanding environments. The manufacturer’s footage shows a larger quadruped platform in action, connecting hardware design with the physical conditions its intended applications may involve.

media.alt: Unitree demonstrates the B1 quadruped in demanding operating conditions

title: Go2 advances the compact quadruped platform
blurb: Unitree introduces Go2 with demonstrations of its compact quadruped platform. The product film brings movement, sensing, and interaction into one presentation, illustrating continued integration of the components needed to make a legged robot usable.

media.alt: Unitree introduces the Go2 compact quadruped

title: G1 moves toward a manufactured humanoid platform
blurb: Unitree presents the G1 version it describes as ready for mass production. The manufacturer’s demonstration shows the humanoid’s movement and mechanical packaging, marking a product-development step toward producing the platform in a repeatable form.

media.alt: Unitree demonstrates the G1 version it describes as ready for mass production

title: R1 broadens the humanoid hardware offering
blurb: Unitree introduces R1 through its original launch film, adding a compact humanoid to its product range. The demonstration presents the platform’s body and movement together, showing how another manufacturer packages humanoid hardware as a complete product.

media.alt: Unitree's original R1 humanoid launch film

title: Inside the making of Atlas
blurb: Boston Dynamics opens the manufacturing process behind Atlas in Machine, Assemble, Repair. The film brings machining and assembly into view, showing the practical work that turns a robot design into physical components and an assembled platform.

media.alt: Boston Dynamics shows machining and assembly used to build Atlas
